minor.issue: 500 Internal Server Error when payload includes 'due_date' (or any datetime.date field). RCA: app/mongo_utils.py::_serialize handled datetime but not date. Pydantic parses ISO date string into datetime.date and pymongo BSON encoder chokes with 'InvalidDocument: cannot encode object: datetime.date(...)'. Fixed by adding isinstance(v, date) branch that returns v.isoformat(). Same helper is used by ~all routers, so fix also benefits any endpoint that emits date-typed fields (FixedCost.start_date/end_date, Investment.start_date, LegalEntity fiscal snapshots, etc.). Post-fix intercompany create returns 200 and correctly persists source+target pair + receivable + payable.

rca of the issue: BUG: intercompany create endpoint returned 500 with error `bson.errors.InvalidDocument: cannot encode object: datetime.date(2026, 12, 31)`. RCA: `IntercompanyCreate` model has `due_date: Optional[date]`. When client posts `"due_date": "2026-12-31"`, Pydantic parses into `datetime.date`. The helper `app/mongo_utils.py::_serialize` only converted `datetime.datetime` to ISO string, leaving `datetime.date` as-is. Motor/pymongo's BSON encoder does NOT natively support `date` (only `datetime`), so `insert_one` raised. FIX: extended `_serialize` with `if isinstance(v, date): return v.isoformat()` (order: datetime check first — since datetime IS-A date in Python, this ordering is required and correct). Also benefits FixedCost.start_date/end_date, Investment.start_date, LegalEntity fiscal snapshots. VERIFIED: post-fix intercompany create returns 200 + persists source, target, receivable, payable correctly; consolidation and reconciliation-report also work. No other change to business logic.
